candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71) (c. 100 BC)

'And on the four sides of the Lord of Spirits I saw four presences, different from those that sleep not, and I learnt their names: for the angel who went with me made known to me their names' — four-archangel theology of presence (parallel to but distinct from the seven-archangel list at 20:1). Tewahedo iconography of Christ surrounded by the four presences (often depicted on the tabot — the ark's tablets in qǝddǝst, the holy of holies) draws on this verse as canonical authority.

candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71) (c. 100 BC)

'And the fourth, who is set over the repentance unto hope of those who inherit eternal life, is named Phanuel' — Phanuel as the angel of repentance. Tewahedo penitential tradition retains Phanuel as a distinctive feast-day commemoration (unique to Ethiopia among the major Christian traditions), with his role as the angel-mediator of the sinner's hope preserved in monastic confession liturgy.
